text.p: Racal Electronics Plc said on Friday that its Data Products group would incur a second half loss in the region of seven million pounds ($11.4 million) which would hit its results.
It said in a statement it was now expecting overall pre-tax profit in excess of 40 million pounds in 1996/97, well below analysts expectations.
Analysts' expectations had centred on pre-tax profits of 53.5 million pounds ($87.4 million), with forecasts ranging from 41 million to 75 million pounds.
The British defence electronics-to-telecoms group made a profit warning before last year's results, leading to a sharp fall in the share price and criticism from some investors.
By 1141 GMT, shares in the company had fallen 26 pence to stand at 251 pence.
Racal said the loss at its Data Products group was due to a delay in the fast frame relay products.
"This resulted in an increase in research and development costs and a reduction in the anticipated revenues in 1996/97 accruing from these new products," said the firm.
It said its two principal businesses -- Managed Network Services and Defence Electronics -- had performed well, "with excellent prospects for future years."
Final results are due on June 3, 1997.
